page: Amazon Web Services r8g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the memory subsystem as a key strength of this instance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, placing in the top 10% of tested systems, and the large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 25% at 189.8 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly in the top 25%. However, CPU encryption capabilities are relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% on the Passmark encryption test. Large language model inference performance is also limited, with prompt processing for medium 7B models falling into the bottom 10% and text generation for small 135M models in the bottom 25%. Most other compute, database, and web serving benchmarks, including Redis SET operations and static web serving, fall within the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.2xlarge offers high memory density per core, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-performance vector extensions. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without hyperthreading interference. This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and data processing tasks, though it is less optimal for cryptographic operations or heavy machine learning inference.
